- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, particularly if price has been trending down.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the following days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0) for 5+ consecutive days, model tends to drift toward mean reversion; adjust forecast toward historical mean of last 7–14 days.
- Model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; lag 1–2 days in adjusting forecasts to sentiment changes.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >5% deviation), check if sentiment was negative recently — if so, model may have overcorrected.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast with sentiment trend only if sentiment is strong and sustained (>3 days).
